tickets.label: Tickets
tickets.description: Multiple ticket types; each type opens a private channel visible to the chosen roles.
tickets.welcome: Hello {user}, your “{type}” ticket is open. Describe your request here, the team will reply. Click “Close ticket” once it’s resolved.

feedback.disabled: ❌ This module is disabled on this server.

error.notype: ❌ This ticket type no longer exists.
error.max: ❌ You already have {max} open ticket(s). Close it before opening a new one.
error.noperm: ❌ I lack the “Manage Channels” permission to create the ticket.
error.create: ❌ Could not create the ticket channel. Check my permissions and the category.

close.confirm: Close this ticket? The channel will be deleted.
close.notFound: ❌ This ticket cannot be found or is already closed.
close.cantClose: ⛔ Only the author, the type staff or an admin can close it.

g0.label: ⚙️ General
g0.description: After any change, republish the panel with the “Publish” button to refresh its buttons.

title.label: Panel title
title.help: The title of the ticket panel.

description.label: Panel description
description.help: The panel's body text. Saying what a ticket should contain — context, screenshots — saves one round trip on every request.

panelChannelId.label: Panel channel
panelChannelId.help: Where the “Open a ticket” panel is published.

mode.label: Ticket type
mode.help: « Private channel » creates a real channel in the chosen category: it survives anything and archives cleanly, but counts against the server's 500-channel limit. « Private thread » creates a thread in the panel's channel: no practical limit, but Discord auto-archives idle threads and they are harder to find later.

categoryId.label: Category for the channels (channel mode)
categoryId.help: The category tickets are created in. A Discord category holds only 50 channels: past that, opening fails. Has no effect in « private thread » mode.

archiveChannelId.label: Channel where transcripts are archived
archiveChannelId.help: When a ticket is closed, the bot drops the full transcript here before deleting the channel. Empty, the conversation disappears with the channel, for good — this is the setting people regret afterwards.

g1.label: 🎫 Ticket types
g1.description: Each type = one button on the panel, with the roles allowed to see and handle it.

types.label: Types
types.help: One button per row on the panel, with the roles allowed to see and handle that type. This is what keeps a « billing » ticket out of sight of the whole moderation team. With no role on a row, only the author and administrators see the ticket. The prefix names the channels (`sup` → `sup-0001`).
